result.title: PID-Gated Continual Prompt Adaptation Under Noisy Feedback
result.summary: Deploying LLM agents in non-stationary environments requires continually revising their instructions as the task drifts, yet rewriting after every reported mistake can turn noisy feedback into persistent errors. This raises an often-overlooked scheduling question in prompt adaptation: when should feedback trigger a lasting instruction update, and at what editor-call cost? Taking inspiration from proportional-integral-derivative (PID) control, we introduce a family of lightweight gates that react to the current error, accumulate evidence over time, and roll back deterioration after an edit. We benchmark these gates against both simple baselines and advanced prompt optimizers (TextGrad and GEPA), over a diverse suite of drifting tasks, LLM parameter sizes, feedback-noise levels, and random seeds. PID-gated continual prompt adaptation yields a more favorable Pareto trade-off between task performance (high accuracy, low error) and editor-call budget than the baselines considered, pointing to control-theoretic scheduling as a simple, general tool for robust prompt adaptation under unreliable feedback.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对非平稳环境下 LLM 智能体的提示适配调度问题，提出受 PID 控制启发的轻量门控，依据当前误差、历史证据积累与编辑后回滚来决定噪声反馈是否触发持久指令更新，并在多类漂移任务、模型规模与噪声水平上与简单基线及 TextGrad、GEPA 比较其性能与编辑调用成本的 Pareto 权衡。
AI.relevance_reason: PID 门控「响应当前误差、累积证据、回滚恶化」的接受/拒绝调度机制，可能可供核查为 LVR 中迭代推理状态何时提交更新、何时停止以及编辑/计算预算分配提供线索，但原文作用于提示层面而非 latent 状态，迁移性待确认。
